Load Balancing Basics: Round Robin vs Least Connections: storyboard

Episode 7 · voice Jessica · 9 scenes · 87.1s (measured timing) · one still per beat, 8 frames after it fires

hook hook Hook · 0.0s–8.0s

Headline: One server? Never.

“One server can't handle the whole world. So what stands in front of millions of users? A load balancer.”

branding sting 8.0s–9.5s

Bite wipe → logos → cut. No voiceover, just the chomp.

idea idea Analogy · 9.5s–18.5s

Headline: The host at the door

“A load balancer is a restaurant host. Guests arrive, and the host sends each one to a table with room.”

breakdown lb FlowDiagram · 18.5s–28.2s

Headline: Spread the load

“Without one, every user piles onto one server, and it melts. With one, users hit the balancer first, and it spreads them across the team.”

breakdown rr FlowDiagram · 28.2s–39.5s

No headline

“Round robin is the simplest: server one, server two, server three, repeat. Fair, but it ignores how busy each one is.”

breakdown lc FlowDiagram · 39.5s–48.5s

Headline: Fewest wins

“Least connections is smarter. A slow request keeps one server busy, so new traffic goes to whoever has the fewest.”

breakdown health FlowDiagram · 48.5s–57.3s

Headline: Skip the dead

“Health checks keep it honest. The balancer pings every server, and when one stops answering, it quietly stops sending traffic there.”

breakdown layers Split · 57.3s–69.4s

Headline: Blind or smart

“Layer four balances by address and port: fast, but blind. Layer seven reads the request itself, so images go one way and checkout another.”

breakdown global Map · 69.4s–81.3s

No headline

“Go global, and DNS sends you to the nearest region first. For the software, NGINX, HAProxy and AWS ALB are the usual picks.”

gist gist GistCard · 81.3s–87.1s

No headline

“That's the gist: spread the traffic, skip the broken, stay up. Follow for more.”
